short: A customisation attached to an ordered item.
seoTitle: Modifier — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A modifier is a customisation attached to an item at ordering — extra cheese, no onion, medium spice, a larger size. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: A modifier is a customisation attached to an item at ordering — extra cheese, no onion, medium spice, a larger size. Modifiers may be free or priced, and priced ones carry their own cost.
bodyHtml:
Why Modifier matters

Modifiers are where accuracy and margin quietly leak. Free add-ons with real ingredient cost erode plate margin, and unrecorded preferences are a leading cause of remakes.

How Modifier works in practice

Define modifiers in the menu structure with their own cost and price rather than as free-text notes, so both the kitchen ticket and the cost report reflect them.

faq.question: Should modifiers be priced?
faq.answer: Anything with meaningful ingredient cost should be, even at a token price, or it drifts into a default expectation.

faq.question: Why not use free-text notes?
faq.answer: Notes are unstructured, so nothing is costed, counted or consistently understood in the kitchen.
